name: Pale Violet
lede: Pale Violet is a light, clear violet, a descriptive phrase that old books apply to flowers and dyes and that our painting archive does not find at all.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Pale violet is [[violet]] lightened, and as a phrase it is older than any one swatch. Paterson uses it to define anemone, which he calls a pale violet, and Persian blue, which he calls a strong blue and a pale violet in the same line [1]. Even the dictionary treats the phrase loosely [1].

Finlay uses it for the edge of the spectrum: Newton could have added a seventh color by splitting pale violet from deep purple, he notes, and chose indigo instead [2]. The library's swatch is ISCC-NBS block 199, a "very light violet", and also appears in the xkcd survey [3]. It is related to [[lavender]], [[lilac]], [[lavender-blue]] and [[anemone]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering at least one per cent of its canvas, as photographed [4]. That describes our archive, not painting as a whole [4]. A light violet this clear is a color of screens and flowers more than of oil paint [4].
